title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Lena Chen
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflow has caused long queue times and made it hard to reason about cache behavior and release automation. This PR splits the pipeline into dedicated lint, test, and release workflows; consolidates shared build matrix logic into a reusable workflow; and optimizes action/cache usage and parallelism for node-based packages.

What changed (high level):
- New workflows: .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml (replaces monorepo ci.yml)
- Introduced .github/workflows/workflow-templates/build-matrix.yml to share matrix generation and node/action pins
- Updated GitHub Actions to latest stable (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4) and pinned key action versions for reproducible behavior
- Standardized Node version matrix to [18, 20] and added fast-fail matrix pruning for docs-only changes
- Reduced redundant cache keys and added restore-keys patterns to improve hit rates across parallel jobs
- Tweak cache concurrency and job parallelism limits for repo-wide heuristics to reduce API throttling incidents
- Improved release automation: separate publish step with explicit gating and additional checks to avoid accidental publishes on dependent repo updates

Why: Split workflows shorten feedback loop for lint failures and make test runs more predictable. Sharing matrix code reduces duplication and eases future upgrades. Cache key cleanup and tuned parallelism reduce frequent cache misses and GitHub Actions rate-limit failures observed in ENG-2147.

Checklist: 
- [x] Split monolithic ci.yml into focused workflows
- [x] Add reusable workflow for build matrix
- [x] Pin actions and upgrade Node versions where safe
- [x] Validate release workflow gating in dry-run
- [x] Run canary on redwood-sdk-* packages

Commits (summary):
- feat(ci): add lint.yml and test.yml, move lint/test jobs out of ci.yml
- chore(ci): add workflow-templates/build-matrix.yml and refactor matrix generation
- chore(deps): bump actions/checkout -> v4, setup-node -> v4; update node toolchain pins
- perf(ci): tighten cache keys and add restore-keys for monorepo packages
- fix(ci): limit parallelism and add retry logic for flaky network steps

Changed files (representative): [".github/workflows/ci.yml (removed or small wrapper)", ".github/workflows/lint.yml (new)", ".github/workflows/test.yml (new)", ".github/workflows/release.yml (new)", ".github/workflows/workflow-templates/build-matrix.yml (new)", "scripts/ci-utils/generate-matrix.js (refactor)", "docs/ci.md (updated)"]

Notes on scope: This does not change any runtime production code. It updates CI infra and developer workflows only. Release automation changes were tested in a dry-run and audited by security before merge.
review_comments: Ravi Patel (reviewer): Nice split — can we ensure that the release workflow requires 'tests: success' and 'lint: success' explicitly? I saw an early draft that gated only on the matrix artifact.
Lena Chen (author): Good catch. Updated release.yml to require both lint and test. Also added a final 'smoke:canary' job that runs only on release tags.
Jordan Myers (reviewer): The new cache keys look cleaner. One ask: add a fallback restore-key for cross-Node-version restores so we don't miss on node patch bumps.
Lena Chen (author): Added restore-keys with node-major prefix; added comment explaining tradeoffs and expected hit rate improvements.
Sabrina Liu (reviewer): Please add an entry to docs/ci.md describing the new developer workflow and how to run the matrix locally.
Lena Chen (author): docs/ci.md updated with examples for running the matrix via scripts/ci-utils. Also included guidance to skip lint for docs-only PRs.
ci_checks: test workflow (ubuntu-latest, node 18/20): flaky -> rerun -> success
release_notes: Split CI into focused workflows (lint, test, release), added reusable build matrix template, upgraded GitHub Actions pins, and optimized cache parallelism and keys to reduce CI latency and flakiness.
notes: Follow-up tasks: monitor cache hit rates for two weeks (ENG-2199), validate that nightly release dry-run passes for dependent repos, and schedule a post-mortem if flakiness > 2% in next 7 days.
risk_assessment: Low: non-runtime changes. Medium operational risk for release automation — mitigated by dry-run and gating.
